Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

To the rider and the driver — this ruling decides DSP-02816 on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger for TRP-02816. ROUTE DEVIATION: NONE. Both sides read the trace the same way and they are right. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of the optimal distance AND 0.8 km. The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-02816, not the rounded 20.6 km convenience copy on the trip record) is 20.58 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km (EV-TRIP-02816) — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%. The percentage limb fails, so no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the distance charge of SGD 14.70 and the time charge of SGD 7.42 stand. THE ERP LINE: REFUNDED IN FULL. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02816) carries one ERP line — AYE Alexandra Rd gantry, SGD 3.00, at lat 1.289647, lng 103.863838. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating a fix within 250 m of it as a crossing; the nearest of the trace's 162 fixes is 330.73 m away (at 11:10:50), outside that radius. The trace is complete — 100.0% coverage, a steady 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c). On the measurement the policy prescribes, that gantry was not crossed. POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge for a gantry the trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists. Amount returned: SGD 3.00. The SGD 0.50 de minimis floor governs POL-RD-02 recomputations and does not trim this correction, and the correction is not netted against distance or time. The disputed amount on file is SGD 5.00, but the claim as pleaded is the SGD 3.00 ERP line and that is what is returned; base fare SGD 3.80, distance SGD 14.70, time SGD 7.42 and platform fee SGD 0.80 all reconcile to the trip record and are properly chargeable. Total charged was SGD 30.55. ARGUMENTS THAT DID NOT SUCCEED. (1) The driver's submission that a 330.73 m closest approach does not prove the path never entered the 250 m circle is rejected: the 250 m radius is the match rule POL-RD-09 itself states, the trace is dense and gap-free, and the gantry carries coordinates, so the 'undecidable, treat as matched' rule for coordinate-less gantries does not apply. (2) The driver's alternative submission succeeds and is reflected in the remedy: the correction is confined to the single line, SGD 3.00, and is a pass-through of a government-set charge rather than a payment by the driver. (3) The driver's statement that 'the ERP is charged by the system' cites no artifact and no clause; under POL-RD-08 an assertion that points to nothing carries no weight, and that a machine raised the line does not answer POL-RD-09(4), which tests the line against the trace. PROFILES. No profile field decides anything here. POL-GEN-01 makes rating, acceptance rate, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and the lifetime prior_* counters context only, and they were not used. The citable counters were checked and neither test engages: driver deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, so POL-RD-06 finds no pattern and no conduct referral follows; rider deviation_claims_60d is 1 with 0 substantiated, so POL-RD-08's reliability factor does not bite. MISSING ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-02816-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact. No party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was unavailable on the record and no closure-adjusted optimal exists; this is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it does not escalate the case. ESCALATION AND EXECUTION. No escalation applies. POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered where the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), the POL-RD-09(4) referral is an addition to this ruling and not an escalation, and nothing in POL-RD-10(1)–(7) fires. Every artifact the ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(2) discount caps confidence and the 0.70 floor is not approached. The monetary effect, SGD 3.00, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 and is executed automatically on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
To both parties. Two questions are in play and the tribunal decides them separately. (1) Route deviation — none. The governing measurement is the GPS trace's own length, 20.58 km (EV-GPS-02816, not the rounded 20.6 km convenience copy on the trip record), against the booked optimal of 19.60 km (EV-TRIP-02816): an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear both 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal; 5.0% fails the percentage limb, so no deviation is established however the trip is characterised, and POL-RD-02 does not run. The distance and time charges therefore stand and no recomputation of the fare is made. Both advocates agree on this and the tribunal adopts it. The trace is also policy-clean — 162 fixes at a steady 10.0 s interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-07's impairment limbs are not met and the deviation question is decided on the trace as measured. (2) The SGD 3.00 ERP line — refunded in full. The fare ledger charges SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' (EV-FARE-02816) and the rider says the vehicle never used that road. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of it as a crossing. Of the trace's 162 fixes the closest to the gantry stands 330.73 m away (fix 128 at 11:10:50), outside the 250 m radius, and the proximity block confirms the closest approach is not taken across a gap (gap_brackets_closest_approach = false, across_gap_distance_m null). On the only test the policy states, the line is a charge for a crossing that did not happen: a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's answer on this point is rejected. The argument that a fix 330.73 m out cannot prove the continuous path never entered the 250 m radius between two 10 s fixes tests the policy's chosen proxy, not the clause. POL-RD-09 states its match rule as a fix within 250 m, and where a match genuinely cannot be run — a gantry carrying no coordinates — it says so and treats the line as matched. It does not make a measured closest approach outside the radius undecidable. The ledger corroborates the defect on its own face: the line is flagged on_optimal_route = false and the optimal route's ERP total is SGD 0.00. The driver's further claims — that no deviation exists, that POL-RD-02 therefore does not run, that the trace is unimpaired, that POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and that if the line is treated as unmatched the correction is confined to the line itself — are all accepted. His statement 'the ERP is charged by the system' cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and is discarded; that a machine raised the line rather than a person is no answer, because POL-RD-09(4) tests the line against the trace and the trace says the gantry was not crossed. The correction is confined to that line and the case does not escalate. The ledger itemises exactly one ERP line, SGD 3.00, against a charged total of SGD 30.55, and every other component (base fare, distance, time, platform fee) has its counterpart in the trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged: POL-RD-09(4) says expressly that it is not triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. The absent traffic advisory does not escalate the case either: EV-ADVIS-02816-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, but no party invoked it as an excuse for the route, so its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged (POL-RD-13(1)). POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record and the driver's traffic position, such as it is, carries nothing. Quantum and confidence. Charged total SGD 30.55; the refund is the SGD 3.00 ERP line; SGD 27.55 of the charge stands, and no driver compensation is due or ordered. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-02816 and EV-FARE-02816, both admissibility-COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the ruling carries no discount and the 0.70 floor is not approached. Every profile entry relied on or mentioned by either side is credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01: the driver's rating, acceptance_rate, prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are context-only fields and none was used as a ground of decision, and the rider's deviation_claims_60d record (1 claim, 0 substantiated) does not engage POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift and neither helps nor hinders her. The monetary effect, SGD 3.00, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.
